collection.source_input: US20090237807A1, the prescription table transcribed in this batch's brief (the brief's table 1 of 17; the publication's own Embodiment 1, confirmed by the stated full length of 7.2464 mm): a 13-surface prescription, surfaces 1-12 with the aperture stop at surface 5 and the image plane at surface 13
collection.redistribution: public patent document; the prescription numbers are transcribed as facts, no source asset is redistributed
collection.attribution: US20090237807A1, Olympus Medical Systems Corp.; the design is cited by publication number and example

title: Endoscope objective lens, US20090237807A1 example 1 (Embodiment 1)

design.example_number_confirmation: the publication numbers its examples 'Embodiment 1' to 'Embodiment 17' in a conditions table, and its prescription tables appear in that order. This is the first prescription table, and it is Embodiment 1: its transcribed spacings sum to 7.2464 mm, which is exactly the 'Full length of lens 7.2464' the publication prints in the first of its seventeen parameter tables

aperture_validity.basis: the aperture stop is a plate in the air space between the second and third lenses (source surface 5, marked (S)), with a 0.1438 mm opening against 0.45 mm clear semi-diameters on the surfaces either side of it
aperture_validity.consequence: the Project's stop limits the cone it passes, so the record may be evaluated against stop-dependent constraints
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: eligibility only: a stop-dependent match needs evidence (a field point or a pupil sample), which this batch does not assert

design.configuration_note: the source states one prescription and one set of first-order values for this example; there is no zoom or focus travel to choose between

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED air wavelength 587.56 nm (the d line, the wavelength the source's refractive index and Abbe number refer to), converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact)
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states indices at the d line only. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; a single d-line index pair does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial effective focal length of the native Project.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial distance from the last optical surface vertex to the rear focal point for collimated input.

total_track_mm.definition: Axial distance from the first optical surface to the image plane.

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length. atol = 0.005 mm is half a unit in the last decimal of the coarsest focal length these publications print (two decimals); rtol = 2e-3 is 1e-3 for a prescription printed to four decimals on radii as small as 0.27 mm plus 1e-3 for the engine's air-referenced index convention

back_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.conditions: the source's parameter table for this example states 'Focal length 1.00000', and its table header states the unit is mm, so the value is 1.00000 mm at the d line
nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.definition: effective focal length of the whole system in air
nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.note: a unit focal length to five decimals in a summary table is a design target rather than a measured focal length, which is why paraxial is NOT_CHECKED below

nominal_back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the paraxial image point
nominal_back_focal_length_mm.note: the source states no back focal length

f_number.definition: image-space f-number as the publication states it
f_number.basis: SOURCE_STATED (the source's parameter table for this example: F number 3.476)

aperture.stop_opening_note: the stop plate's clear semi-diameter in the CSV is 0.1438 mm = 1.00000/(2*3.476), so the modelled stop reproduces the source's stated F-number. The aperture fact itself is the source's, not derived from the model

paraxial_working_f_number.definition: Reciprocal of twice the admitted axial marginal ray's reduced image angle.

field.definition: the source states a half-angle of view
field.basis: SOURCE_STATED (the source's parameter table for this example: Half-angle of view 63.75045 deg; the full field is twice the stated half field, DERIVED)
field.image_height_basis: SOURCE_STATED (the source's parameter table for this example: 'An image height 0.932')
field.convention_note: the source states both a 63.75045 deg half angle of view and an image height of 0.932 mm. With the engine's 1.001119 mm focal length a distortion-free system would put the chief ray at f*tan(63.75) = 2.03 mm, and an equidistant projection would give 1.11 mm, so the stated image height is only consistent with the stated angle if the objective is strongly barrel-distorted (f*sin(63.75) = 0.90 mm is the closest simple projection) or if the two are stated under different conditions. Recorded as the source states both, not resolved

model_glasses.name: G188815
model_glasses.basis: surfaces 1 and 6 of the source table state nd 1.88815 and vd 40.76; a constant index at the stated nd, since two numbers do not define a dispersion curve

model_glasses.name: G193429
model_glasses.basis: surfaces 3 and 9 of the source table state nd 1.93429 and vd 18.90; a constant index at the stated nd

model_glasses.name: G159143

model_glasses.name: G151825

materials.policy: Every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd. A patent table gives nd and vd only, which cannot define a dispersion curve; fitting one would invent a material. Published catalog glasses were looked up as a cross-check and are recorded under catalog_comparisons, never substituted.
materials.catalog_comparison_note: catalog_version 2026-11-25.1 of the engine's glass index, d line. None of the four pairs has a published glass within 5e-5 in nd and 0.05 in vd; the closest are listed with their differences. The lookup is a cross-check only: every material in the Project is the source's own constant index

approximations.detail: every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd; the source's Abbe number is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour and chromatic focal shift are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the d line only

the source states no clear apertures. The axial beam radius is EFL/(2*F#) = 1.00000/(2*3.476) = 0.144 mm, and the stop opening is set to exactly that so the modelled stop reproduces the source's stated F-number. The clear apertures then follow the prescription's own geometry: 0.45 mm over the three front elements (0.9 mm clear diameter, the small-diameter class a 127-degree endoscope objective needs), 0.50-0.60 mm over the rear cemented pair, and 1.00 mm over the final cover plate so it can carry the source's stated 0.932 mm image height. mech_semi_diameter is 0.02 mm beyond the clear aperture. These set the stop plate and the solid checks and do not enter the first-order values

the source's object row states a surface interval of 13.5000 mm; the Project is built for that finite conjugate, not for infinity. With it, the axial image of that object lands 0.015 mm beyond the source's image plane, 0.2 % of the 7.2464 mm track, which is the order of the table's four-decimal rounding
the source gives no stop-plate outer radius; the plate reaches 0.47 mm, a little beyond the 0.45 mm clear semi-diameter of the surfaces either side of it

nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled. The prescription is spherical and plane only: the publication prints no conic or aspheric coefficient table for this example

notes: project check accepted the committed Project with os-optics 0.14.0

project solids reported no error-severity finding. It reports EDGE_THICKNESS_IMPLAUSIBLE at INFO severity on all five elements, which is what a prescription whose glass is 0.37-1.37 mm thick on a 0.9-2.0 mm clear aperture produces; the severity is INFO and the status is VALID

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED: the source states a focal length (1.00000 mm) but no back focal length, and MATCHED needs both. Its unit focal length to five decimals is also a design target rather than a measured value. For information, the engine's 1.001119 mm lands 0.112 % above it, outside the 1e-5 + 1e-4*scale rule; about 0.06 % of that is the engine's air-referenced index convention and the rest is the source's four-decimal rounding. No value was tuned

the transcription is self-consistent with the source twice over: the transcribed spacings sum to 7.2464 mm, exactly the publication's stated 'Full length of lens 7.2464', and the Project's image plane is at that same 7.2464 mm from the first vertex. The axial image of the stated 13.5 mm object lands 0.015 mm beyond the source's image plane

the source's stated 63.75045 deg half field and 0.932 mm image height are not mutually consistent with the engine's focal length under any simple projection (see field.convention_note); both are recorded as stated and the mismatch is left open
no field verification: this batch built no per-field configurations, so no field-dependent quantity is asserted

record_hash_method: SHA-256 over this record's JSON with the record_hash and record_hash_method members removed: json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) encoded as UTF-8, no trailing newline. Recompute it from the committed record.json after parsing the JSON, not from the file's bytes.
